title: Digital Twin-Based Intrusion Detection for Vehicle Powertrain CAN Bus Systems
abstract: arXiv:2608.17093v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing automotive intrusion detection systems (IDSs) for the Controller Area Network (CAN) largely target discrepancies in message timing, frequency, or sequencing and cannot detect attacks that preserve these properties while manipulating the payload. Digital twins (DTs) have been used to emulate CAN traffic and generate attack scenarios for IDS evaluation, but their use for intrusion detection remains unexplored. This study develops a DT-based IDS that jointly models physical relationships among decoded powertrain signals and identifies attacks through residuals between predicted and observed behavior. A shared-encoder LSTM DT was trained on 17 decoded signals from a real Hyundai/Kia CAN log to jointly predict seven numeric and two categorical gear signals over a 24-step window. A timestep is flagged when a residual exceeds a calibrated threshold, while adaptive rollout protects the twin's input history from sustained contamination

translated_title: 基于数字孪生的车辆动力总成CAN总线系统入侵检测
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17093v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：现有的针对控制器局域网（CAN）的汽车入侵检测系统（IDS）主要关注消息时间、频率或序列的差异，无法检测那些在保持这些属性不变的同时操纵负载的攻击。数字孪生（DT）已被用于模拟CAN流量并生成攻击场景以评估IDS，但其在入侵检测中的应用尚未探索。本研究开发了一种基于DT的IDS，该IDS联合建模解码后的动力总成信号之间的物理关系，并通过预测行为与观测行为之间的残差来识别攻击。一个共享编码器LSTM数字孪生模型在来自真实现代/起亚CAN日志的17个解码信号上进行训练，以在24步窗口内联合预测七个数值和两个分类齿轮信号。当残差超过校准阈值时，该时间步被标记，而自适应滚动保护孪生模型的输入历史免受持续污染。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于数字孪生的入侵检测系统，通过联合建模动力总成信号物理关系并利用LSTM预测残差，有效检测保持消息时序属性但操纵负载的CAN总线攻击。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a digital twin-based intrusion detection system that jointly models physical relationships among powertrain signals and uses LSTM prediction residuals to effectively detect CAN bus attacks that preserve timing properties while manipulating payloads.
